rubric: Every field has a visible label that stays on screen, not a placeholder standing in for a label.
Each error message sits next to the field it belongs to, says in plain words what to fix, and does not rely on colour alone.
What the person already typed is kept, and the password requirements are visible without having to fail first.
The form is a single clear column with one primary button and a sensible order and grouping of fields.
Inputs are easy to see and use: visible borders, comfortable height and legible text size.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B shows the password rule ('At least 8 characters') before anyone gets it wrong, and its error messages start with 'Error:' and an icon, so they don't rely on colour. A's form is polished and fully visible, but you only learn the 10-character password rule after failing. B's screenshot cuts off before the submit button, so its layout can't be fully checked. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers have persistent labels, errors placed under the right fields with icons and plain wording, kept input values and clear bordered inputs.
